style: A square 1:1 food photograph (1024x1024) for a travel guidebook series of 100 Indian and Sri Lankan street dishes. Every image in the series uses this exact setup: camera at a 45-degree overhead angle; the food centered and filling about 60% of the frame; a warm light-oak wooden table, bare, and nothing else on the table unless described; soft natural daylight from the upper left, gentle soft shadows, bright and airy, warm cozy color grading; the far side of the table fades into a soft blur. Serve each dish in the vessel described (steel plate, banana leaf, leaf bowl, unglazed clay cup); otherwise plain off-white stoneware. Paper wrappers and cones are plain brown paper with no print. No hands, no people. No cloth of any kind: no napkin, no handkerchief, no tablecloth, no placemat, no tea towel, no fabric under or beside the subject; the bare wooden table only. Absolutely no text anywhere: no letters, no numbers, no words, no labels, no signs with writing, no logos, no watermark.

cover.draw: Wide landscape illustration (3:2) in the island's warm hand-painted style: a lively Mumbai street-food stall at dusk, a big iron wok of golden frying potato fritters, stacks of soft bread rolls, small glasses of steaming milky tea, warm hanging bulbs, a few cheerful passers-by. In the foreground Ayato stands in front of the stall seen from behind, drawn the same way as on the island's other covers. Keep the top third a calm dusk sky for the title, which we bake ourselves. No text, no signboards with writing.

map.draw: A picture map of India and Sri Lanka in the island's warm hand-painted style, traced over OpenStreetMap coastlines and borders. Five regions in five soft colours: north India (wheat gold), west India (peanut brown), east India (mustard yellow), south India (coconut white with banana-leaf green), Sri Lanka (red-rice red). One tiny food icon per region (naan, vada pav, fish curry, dosa, hopper). A thin dotted travel line linking the 13 route cities in order. No text, no legend, no compass letters, no title.
